title: Fascia Rot From a Full Gutter
description: A gutter packed with oak leaves sends Houston rain behind the fascia board. The shingles above can be fine while the wood at the eave turns soft.
html:
The ceiling is dry. The paint on the fascia is bubbling in a line, and the gutter pulls away when you tug it. That is often not a roof leak. It is water that overtopped a clogged gutter and ran back into the wood the gutter is screwed to. Houston oaks fill a gutter in a season. The roof above it can still be doing its job.

The path the water takes

A clear gutter catches what comes off the drip edge and carries it to the downspout. A gutter full of leaves becomes a trough that overflows at the back, between the gutter and the fascia. The fascia stays wet, the soffit stains, and the hangers loosen. Give it a few years and the board is soft, the gutter is hanging from the roof edge, and now the water is getting under the starter course. That is when a gutter problem becomes a roof problem. Catching it at the paint bubble is cheaper.

Downspouts matter as much as the trough. A downspout that ends in a clogged drain, or a run of gutter with no slope, overflows in the same spot every storm. You can see the stripe on the bed or the siding. Cleaning once a year, and after oak drop, is maintenance. It is not a roof replacement.

What we repair, and what we do not pretend

If the starter and the deck edge are sound, you need the gutter cleared, the hangers reset, and the fascia replaced where it is soft. A painter covering rotten wood is how you buy the same job twice. If the water has already wicked into the deck, then we are in roof repair: drip edge, starter, and the soft sheets at the eave. We will not sell you a field of shingles for a gutter that needed a scoop.

Stand at the downspout during the next hard rain, or call us and we will look at the eave on a roof inspection. (281) 541-0027 or request it here.
